tools.description:
The one write of the decision graph: a batch of ops, applied in order and committed together, or refused whole with nothing written. Each op is checked against the graph the earlier ops left, so add a component before its decisions and a decision before those that depend on it. A refusal names the first op at fault (`op`), the argument (`field`) and the `rule`.
Ops (`op` tag): record a decision (always `proposed`; carries `origin`); revise any of its fields, a list whole or by `add_*`/`remove_*` (never both for one list); rename (rewrites every edge to it); merge `absorbed` into `survivor` (its edges, anchors and tags join the survivor, its text is dropped); remove (refused while decisions depend on it, unless `repoint_to` names their new target); add_component, revise_component, rename_component, remove_component (refused while in use).
Refused too: a revise that changes nothing, an edge to a missing node or to itself, an edge that closes a depends_on cycle. Revising the choice, reason or alternatives of an accepted decision proposes the new text and keeps the accepted one; revising back accepts it again.
Quality: each field a record, revise or merge changes meets the bar: built in, a one-line choice of at most 200 bytes, a reason of real text, an alternative and an anchor at least, no hidden character in any text; then `[quality]` in project.toml. A `warn` pattern and a likely duplicate write the batch and warn in the result.
The result names each op's node and what it changed, never the texts.

duplicates.description: Each decision the batch recorded or whose choice or reason it revised that has likely duplicates, decisions whose choice and reason have a TF-IDF cosine of 0.5 or more with its own, in the order of the ops: a warning, never a refusal.

decision.description: The decision the batch recorded or whose choice or reason it revised, by its name after the batch.

nearest.description: Its likely duplicates, best first, at most three.

score.description: The TF-IDF cosine of the two choices and reasons, to six decimals.

more_duplicates.description: Decisions with likely duplicates not listed in `duplicates`. `status` ranks the pairs under `lint`: the section lists the best pairs; the ones left out rank at or below the last listed, and come into view as the listed ones are settled (merged, or revised apart).

repoint_to.description: Where a remove pointed the edges to its decision.

rewrote.description: Files of other nodes it rewrote: edges repointed, a component's decisions and connections renamed.

status.description: The decision's new status, when the op changed it.

patterns.description: The message of each pattern a warning names, once.

removed.description: Files removed, a rename's old file included.

truncated.description: Present only when the result was cut to fit the result budget: each cut, by JSON pointer, with what it omitted.

warnings.description: What the batch wrote but a `warn` pattern of `[quality]` warns of: each pattern's first match per op, and the first of the origin's and of each op's, in the order of the ops and the patterns; an op's `more_warnings` counts the rest.

at.description: The byte offset of the match in the argument's text.

written.description: Files written, a rename's new file included.

tools.title: Apply

tools.description: The decision graph at a glance: its counts, the write rules `[quality]` in project.toml adds to the built-in ones (counted), the validation issues it holds, what a shared graph's history lacks, the decisions of each component, and `lint`: the best pairs of likely duplicate decisions (a TF-IDF cosine of choice and reason of 0.5 or more), each rule of the quality bar a stored decision breaks, and the decisions whose anchors all name a file and no symbol, counted by kind. The call judges the bar's limits; `section: "lint"` also judges its patterns, a `warn` pattern's included, over the decisions by name within a work limit: `counts.lint.patterns` says how many decisions they read and names in `next` the first left unread, and the same call with `from` set to it reads on from there. Each section fits the result budget; one that leaves items out gives `omitted` and `more`, which says where the rest is. `section` returns one section with the whole budget. `origin` narrows the counts and the findings to the decisions recorded under it. Where the graph sits in the project's git is reported by `trurlic check`.

from.description: With `section: "lint"`: the quality findings of the decisions named this or after, the `[quality]` patterns reading on from here: a previous call's `counts.lint.patterns.next`.

origin.description: Count only the decisions recorded under this origin.

work.description: The patterns' work over every decision and the bound, in state-bytes: the bytes each pattern reads times its NFA's states.

measured.description: The patterns' work over every decision.

tools.description: Get the architectural context for a component: its decisions, the project-wide rules, the decisions of connected components and of what its decisions depend on, and an authoritative brief for coding agents. Use depth="constraints" for a compact brief of choices only.

depth.description: full (default): complete context with reasoning. constraints: choice text only, compact brief, no related decisions.

tools.name: get_context

tools.description: Reverse lookup: given a file or directory path, find every decision anchored there: on the file itself, on a file under the directory, or on a directory that holds the file. Returns decisions sorted by component then name, each with its matching anchors. Project-wide rules apply everywhere and are not listed unless anchored there; get_context("project") lists them.

file.description: File or directory path relative to the project root (e.g. 'src/store/load.rs' or 'src/store'). A leading './' is dropped; backslashes, '..' and absolute paths are refused.
